question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed experimental Claws package lifecycle and its cross-owner OpenClaw/ClawHub rollout as the product direction for portable complete-agent packages?
rationale: The branch is a coherent RFC and does not expose a narrow mechanical defect, but it introduces a new package and manifest model whose lifecycle, compatibility boundary, and rollout ownership require maintainer product sponsorship.

options.title: Approve scoped experimental RFC
options.body: Accept the Claws direction behind the existing experimental gates, with the listed implementation stack reviewed and landed incrementally by the relevant owners.

options.title: Request a narrower RFC
options.body: Keep the proposal open but reduce or defer one or more lifecycle owners, such as portable MCP or shared package cleanup, before approving the contract.

options.title: Decline core roadmap adoption
options.body: Do not adopt this cross-owner package model in core now and leave any future package workflow to a separately sponsored proposal.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped experimental RFC
recommendation.body: Accept the Claws direction behind the existing experimental gates, with the listed implementation stack reviewed and landed incrementally by the relevant owners.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recorded review comments focus on the central naming and MCP ownership questions that a product-direction decision must resolve.
